problem: Existing zero-shot object-goal navigation methods lack a unified visual representation, so spatial-semantic joint matching is complex and inefficient. Multistage frameworks (Visual Perception then Policy Learning) also fail to use historical visual features, which weakens the link between perception and decision-making.
motivation: Agents must find unseen target objects in novel environments using only visual observations and a target representation. A unified, adaptive embedding plus explicit memory of past trajectories and target positions could make matching cheaper and decisions better informed.
key_idea: Learn a unified spatial-semantic embedding via bilinear similarity and dynamic attention, add a target-oriented multiscale memory branch, and train an RL policy with a reward balancing distance, view angle and target relevance.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract implies that unifying the spatial-semantic representation and feeding history into the policy are the sources of the gains.
method: Similarity-aware module (SAM): learns adaptive spatial-semantic embeddings using bilinear similarity metrics and dynamic attention
Target-oriented memory-augmented (TOMA) branch: explicitly encodes historical trajectories and target positions via multiscale aggregation
RL policy: optimized with a reward function balancing distance, view angle, and target relevance
Multistage paradigm (S2AN-ASPM): perception stage followed by policy learning, with memory linking the two

setting.backbone: S2AN-ASPM (SAM + TOMA + RL policy); specific encoders not stated in abstract
